title: The Briar at the Stone Circle
story: On the windy moor, Thurlbane has wrapped the old stone gate in 63 iron thorns, trapping a shepherd and her whole flock inside the circle. Mr 6 tests one sweep of his sword: it shears away 9 thorns, and instantly 4 new ones sprout with a nasty creak. Mr 6 sits on a rock and thinks — because if the briar ever runs out of thorns entirely, there is nothing left to sprout from.
question: If each sweep shears up to 9 thorns and 4 sprout back only when thorns remain, how many sweeps does Mr 6 need to clear all 63 thorns?
solution: Every sweep that leaves thorns behind changes the count by 9 - 4 = 5 fewer thorns.
He wants 9 or fewer thorns left for one finishing sweep: (63 - 9) ÷ 5 = 10.8, so 11 sweeps bring it to 63 - 55 = 8 thorns.
That last sweep clears all 8, so 11 + 1 = 12 sweeps.
praise: Tracking the net loss of 5 thorns per sweep was exactly the right thinking — the final sweep, where nothing grows back, is the step that's easy to miss.
hint: Work out the net change per sweep first, then ask how few thorns must be left so one last sweep can finish them all.
victory: The iron briar unwound with a sulky rattle and the gate swung open for every last sheep; Thurlbane, now just a twig, agreed to grow blackberries instead.
imagePrompt: A numeral-six knight in a little helmet calmly counts glinting iron thorns coiled around an ancient standing-stone gate on a windswept moonlit moor, a shepherd and her flock peering out from inside the circle.
